jobs.description:
About Marvell
Marvell’s semiconductor solutions are the essential building blocks of the data infrastructure that connects our world. Across enterprise, cloud and AI, and carrier architectures, our innovative technology is enabling new possibilities.

At Marvell, you can affect the arc of individual lives, lift the trajectory of entire industries, and fuel the transformative potential of tomorrow. For those looking to make their mark on purposeful and enduring innovation, above and beyond fleeting trends, Marvell is a place to thrive, learn, and lead.

Your Team, Your Impact

The next generation of AI infrastructure depends on how efficiently data moves. As cloud providers expand their AI clusters, optical connectivity is essential to delivering the bandwidth, reach, and power efficiency these systems demand.

Marvell’s Cloud Optics organization develops the advanced optical technologies that help make this expansion possible. Our portfolio spans connectivity within data centers, across campuses, and between data centers—including PAM4 optical digital signal processors (DSPs), coherent-lite DSPs, co-packaged optical engines, and data center interconnect (DCI) optical modules.

Join a team working at the intersection of silicon photonics, advanced semiconductor design, packaging, and system integration. Here, you will help turn complex engineering innovations into production-ready solutions that enable cloud and AI infrastructure to scale.
What You Can Expect
As a Sr. Staff Hardware Engineer – Program Manager, you will own the execution of complex hardware optical programs from initial planning through qualification, customer sampling, and production ramp. This is not management for a single chip development; you will manage multiple concurrent hardware development lines all culminating into a single module product. You will connect technical ambition with disciplined delivery, aligning engineering and business teams around a clear path to successful hardware product introduction.

Your ownership extends beyond an individual silicon tapeout. You will orchestrate the interdependent activities required to deliver complete optical solutions, bringing together photonics, analog design, packaging, validation, supply planning, operations, and finance.Your decisions will help teams resolve technical and operational challenges, protect critical milestones, and deliver the connectivity needed for increasingly demanding AI workloads. This is a high-visibility opportunity to influence product execution, partner with technical leaders, and communicate directly with senior executives.
- - Own end-to-end hardware program delivery. Lead program initiation, strategic planning, tracking, and execution through Marvell’s Product and IP Lifecycle Processes, from concept to production readiness and ramp.
- Build an integrated execution plan. Translate product requirements and engineering objectives into actionable schedules, resource plans, milestones, and measurable deliverables.
- Lead cross-functional alignment. Coordinate photonics design, analog design, packaging, TO/FO, hardware manufacturing, design validation testing (DVT), reliability qualification, planning and supply management, operations, and finance across multiple development sites.
- Manage concurrent development efforts. Align silicon subsystems, optical engines, and final product deliverables while resolving competing priorities and resource constraints.
- Drive critical product milestones. Establish readiness criteria and track progress through test and evaluation, reliability qualification, customer sampling, production acceptance, and ramp.
- Anticipate and mitigate risks. Identify schedule, technical, material, and resource risks early; assign mitigation owners; and drive timely resolution and escalation.
- Manage program dependencies. Track internal and external interdependencies, surface misalignments, and coordinate corrective actions before they affect delivery.
- Create clear accountability. Lead weekly cross-functional reviews and regular program updates, maintaining visibility into decisions, commitments, open issues, and recovery plans.
- Communicate with precision. Deliver concise reports and executive presentations that explain program health, milestone changes, business implications, and decisions needed.
- Guide execution tradeoffs. Partner with engineering and business leaders to balance performance, quality, cost, schedule, and customer requirements.
- Work alongside the team in Santa Clara. This full-time position requires office attendance five days per week; remote and hybrid arrangements are not available.

At Marvell, you will combine meaningful program ownership with exposure to advanced optical and semiconductor technologies. You will work closely with specialists across disciplines, strengthen your technical leadership, and see your efforts progress from early development into products supporting cloud and AI infrastructure at scale.

What We're Looking For
- Bachelor’s degree in Electrical Engineering, Computer Science, or a related technical field; a master’s degree or PhD is a plus.
- Substantial relevant industry experience, preferably 10+ years with a bachelor’s degree, 8+ years with a master’s degree, or 6+ years with a PhD .
- 5+ years of hardware project or program management experience in the semiconductor industry , with demonstrated ownership of complex development programs.
- Proven ability to manage multiple concurrent efforts and deliver both silicon subsystems and complete customer products.
- Technical fluency sufficient to engage engineering teams, understand development dependencies, and guide informed execution decisions.
- Exceptional leadership, organizational, and time management skills, with the ability to motivate geographically distributed teams and influence without direct authority.
- Strong risk identification, analysis, and problem-solving capabilities, including experience developing mitigation and recovery plans.
- Sound judgment in balancing internal business objectives with customer requirements.
- Excellent written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to present complex program information clearly to engineering teams and executives.
- Experience with Primavera P6, Microsoft Project, or comparable program management software.
- Proficiency with PowerPoint, Excel, Agile, and Jira.
- A collaborative approach, strong follow-through, and a track record of creating clarity and accountability across functions.

Experience that will help you stand out:
- Background in optical connectivity, silicon photonics, high-speed interconnects, or advanced semiconductor packaging.
- Experience coordinating hardware validation, reliability qualification, new product introduction, and production ramp.
- Familiarity with material readiness, supply constraints, and the operational dependencies involved in bringing optical or semiconductor products to market.
- Bring your technical perspective and program leadership to Marvell—and help deliver the optical connectivity that enables the next wave of cloud and AI innovation.

jobs.description:
About Marvell
Marvell’s semiconductor solutions are the essential building blocks of the data infrastructure that connects our world. Across enterprise, cloud and AI, and carrier architectures, our innovative technology is enabling new possibilities.

At Marvell, you can affect the arc of individual lives, lift the trajectory of entire industries, and fuel the transformative potential of tomorrow. Your Team, Your Impact

Marvell's custom silicon programs succeed only if supply chain delivers them on schedule. The AVP, Supply Chain Program Management owns that outcome, from program approval through production ramp and end of life.

Why now
• Demand is scaling fast. Advanced-node wafer demand is projected to grow roughly 5x over the next five years.
• The program pipeline is expanding every year, with more programs running concurrently at every stage from business development to production.
• Cycles are compressing. Product refresh timelines are moving from 24 to 12 months, so NPI and production ramps overlap.
• Programs are first-of-a-kind: new packaging (2.5D/3D, CoWoS, MCM), long substrate and HBM lead times, and hyperscaler customers who expect a single accountable owner.
What You Can Expect
WHAT YOU WILL OWN

1. Lead the SCPM organization
- Build and lead a team of Program Managers, organized by hyperscaler customer and program portfolio.

- Set one operating model: roles, hand-offs, governance, and standards.

- Hire, develop, and retain senior program talent, and scale team capacity ahead of five-year demand growth.

2. End-to-end program delivery, PA to EOL
- Own the supply chain plan of record for every hyperscaler program: schedule, cost, capacity, and customer experience.

- Shape supply terms in RFPs and SOWs. Own supply chain program schedule development.

- Drive pre-tape-out readiness: sample requirements, component forecasts (wafers, HBM, substrate, OSAT), capacity allocation, test capacity, and sourcing decisions.

- Run post-tape-out execution through production readiness, ramp, sustaining production, and EOL.

3. Be the executive voice of supply chain to customers
- Co-plan directly with customer supply chain teams on business model, allocation, consignment, and delivery.

- Serve as senior escalation point for customer-critical programs and recovery efforts.

- Build trusted executive relationships with foundry, OSAT, substrate, and memory partners.

4. Govern with rigor
- Enforce milestone integrity, risk and issue escalation, and exec-review readiness.

- Partner with Engineering Program Managers, PMO, BU leadership, NPI Execution, and Operations (PE, TE, Quality) as a single integrated program team.

- Hold the line on clean hand-offs between SCPM, NPI Execution, and BU Planning.

5. Scale through process, systems, and data
- Standardize program tooling, templates, and dashboards.

- Drive adoption of Kinaxis, Lima, Snowflake, and Power BI to replace spreadsheet-based NPI planning.

- Use AI and automation to cut manual reporting and speed decisions.

HOW SUCCESS IS MEASURED
- Time to revenue

- Programs delivered within plan of record

- Customer satisfaction scores

- Supply chain KPIs: DOI, CRD performance, OSD

- Team health: retention, bench strength, role clarity

WHO YOU PARTNER WITH
Chief Supply Chain Officer and staff · BU General Managers · Engineering Program Managers and PMO · NPI Execution and Master Data · BU Planning and Central Planning · Procurement · Operations (PE, TE, Quality) · Foundry, OSAT, substrate, and memory suppliers · Customer supply chain executives

What We're Looking For
WHAT YOU BRING

Must have
- Bachelor's degree in Supply Chain, Industrial Engineering, Operations, or related field. Master's or MBA preferred.

- 15+ years in semiconductor supply chain, program management, or operations. 7+ years leading managers or senior ICs.

- Proven ownership of complex, multi-party programs from design win through high-volume manufacturing.

- Hands-on knowledge of advanced packaging, foundry, OSAT, and substrate supply chains.

- Executive presence with hyperscaler or large strategic customers.

- Strong analytical judgment and clear, concise written and verbal communication.

Strongly preferred
- Custom ASIC or XPU program experience, including first-of-a-kind builds.

- Experience with Kinaxis, Oracle ERP, Power BI, or comparable planning tools.

- Track record building or restructuring a program management function.
